newsitem.title: UK: LDC debt slumbers through London holiday period.
newsitem.headline: LDC debt slumbers through London holiday period.

text.p: Emerging debt prices hovered around new York closing levels in London, with little news to stir a market becalmed amid the Chistmas holiday break, dealers said.
"There's absolutely nothing going on," said one trader at a major UK firm here.
East European debt prices were mostly flat though one trader said Russian Vnesh paper firmed a touch following President Boris Yeltsin's return to work.
Dollar Vnesh loans traded 1/8 higher at 79-00, he said, but this was about the only credit to stir across the emerging debt market.
Peruvian paper was unchanged as the hostage crisis wore on, with some 104 captives still imprisoned in the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima. Peru Citi bonds were flat at 116-00.

Players were steering clear of Bulgaria which has been without a prime minister since Saturday. A new premier may not officially be announced until after parliament holds an extraordinary session on December 28.
Some Latin American investors were awaiting a speech by former Argentine economy minister Domingo Cavallo, due to be televised later on Friday, but the trader said prices were steady.
Bulgarian IABs were flat at 51-1/2 while Argentine FRBs held steady at 87-1/8, in line with yesterday's U.S. market close.
Players said they were hoping next week would see an influx of fresh cash for the start of the 1997 trading year. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
